explanation: French table manners place strong emphasis on eating quietly and with restraint, so slurping is considered uncouth across casual bistros and formal restaurants alike. This applies to noodles as it does to soup or any dish — audible eating noises are seen as a lack of self-control at the table, not a compliment to the cook.
local_tip: Twirl noodles discreetly onto your fork (using a spoon to help, if offered) and eat without audible suction, the same way you'd eat pasta.

also_check.note: Slurping noodles is a sign of enjoyment and also helps cool hot noodles while eating.
Slurping is generally acceptable and can signal enjoyment of the meal, though norms vary by region and setting.
Slurping pasta is considered poor manners; it should be eaten quietly, twirled onto a fork.

sources.title: 27 Do's and Don'ts at the French Table
